raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash can compile mHC prenorm kernels during eager prefill, delaying requests. This change uses the existing prewarm helper during model load so those kernels can be compiled before serving.

The benefit depends on startup settings. With breakable prefill graphs and the `prefill_shapes` warmup, main already compiles every mHC prenorm kernel before readiness. Without those settings, the hook trades longer startup for fewer cold first-request stalls.

## Modifications

Call the shared prewarm helper after GLM loads, using the first mHC layer and the same parameters as forward, including fused input normalization. For CPU-offloaded layers, temporarily stage the required tensors on the rank's CUDA device while leaving the original parameters offloaded.

Skip inactive CUDA/mHC configurations, encoder-only instances and disabled chunked prefill. NextN does not use this hook.

## Accuracy Tests

The registered prewarm GPU suite and scoped formatting pass on the updated branch on an RTX 5070 Ti (SM120). The suite exercises the production load wrapper and real TileLang kernels, compares forward results with Torch, and checks that a warmed forward compiles no additional kernel. It covers full and partial CPU offload while preserving the original parameter storage.

A TP4 B200 server run at revision b212f59552 confirmed that the hook ran on all ranks and the TileLang cache was complete at readiness. It predates the latest base update and the later CPU-offload staging change. The updated branch has not had a B200 server run.

Run the model prewarm tests with `python -m pytest` in a compatible CUDA environment or through the registered CI runner.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The cold-start comparison used a GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 model on TP4 B200, with empty caches and a main nightly at commit 7224fce1b5e4. The PR arm overlaid the hook from b212f59552; it predates the latest base update and did not include the later CPU-offload staging change.

| Startup configuration | Start time, main / hook | TTFT sweep, cold / warm (main) | TTFT sweep, cold / warm (hook) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Breakable prefill graphs and `prefill_shapes` warmup | 678 s / 682 s | 1.65 s / 1.40 s | 1.73 s / 1.41 s |
| No prefill graphs or warmup | 630 s / 664 s | 32.70 s / 1.44 s | 10.32 s / 1.40 s |

With warmup enabled, main already has the mHC kernels ready, so the hook adds about four seconds to startup without a measurable TTFT change. Without warmup, the hook reduces the cold sweep by about 22 seconds while adding 34 seconds to startup. DeepGEMM and Triton compilation stalls remain. Each arm ran once per configuration, except for the repeat of main in the first configuration.

TP8, other GPUs, warm-disk startup, CPU offload on B200 and a current-head B200 server run remain unvalidated.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stage CPU-offloaded mHC weights before prewarming**

When `--cpu-offload-gb` is set, `OffloaderV1` moves the decoder layer's direct mHC parameters to CPU during `make_layers`; deriving the residual device here and passing those parameters directly bypasses the layer's functional-call onload wrapper. +import importlib
+import weakref
+from contextlib import nullcontext
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm import mhc
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.layers.utils.common import PPMissingLayer
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.model_runner_components.load_model_utils import (
+    maybe_precompile_model_kernels_after_loading,
+)
+from sglang.srt.models.glm5_next import (
+    Glm5NextDecoderLayer,
+    Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration,
+)
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel, publish, reset_context
+from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
+from sglang.srt.utils.offloader import OffloaderV1
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=90, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+
+def _make_mhc_model(sinkhorn_iters=20):
+    config = SimpleNamespace(
+        mhc=True,
+        hc_mult=4,
+        hidden_size=4096,
+        rms_norm_eps=1e-6,
+        hc_eps=1e-6,
+        hc_sinkhorn_iters=sinkhorn_iters,
+    )
+    layer = Glm5NextDecoderLayer.__new__(Glm5NextDecoderLayer)
+    torch.nn.Module.__init__(layer)
+    layer.config = config
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    layer.hc_attn_fn = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(24, 16384, device="cuda") * 0.001)
+    layer.hc_attn_scale = torch.nn.Parameter(
+        torch.tensor([0.5, 0.25, 0.25], device="cuda")
+    )
+    layer.hc_attn_base = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(24, device="cuda"))
+    layer.input_layernorm = torch.nn.Module()
+    layer.input_layernorm.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(
+        torch.rand(4096, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") + 0.5
+    )
+    layer.input_layernorm.variance_epsilon = 1e-6
+    model = Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration.__new__(Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration)
+    torch.nn.Module.__init__(model)
+    model.config = config
+    model.model = SimpleNamespace(layers=[PPMissingLayer(), layer])
+    return model, layer
+
+
+def test_glm_mhc_prewarm_covers_forward_kernels(monkeypatch):
+    """A prefill must not compile a new mHC kernel after the load hook warmed it."""
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA is required for mHC prewarm")
+
+    publish(
+        ServerArgs(model_path="dummy", device="cuda", chunked_prefill_size=8192),
+        role="test",
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mhc, "use_symmetric_memory", lambda *a, **kw: nullcontext())
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mhc, "is_allocation_symmetric", lambda: False)
+    model, layer = _make_mhc_model()
+    jit = importlib.import_module("tilelang.jit")
+
+    try:
+        with (
+            get_parallel().override(tp_group=None),
+            envs.SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE.override(True),
+            patch.object(jit, "compile", wraps=jit.compile) as compile_kernel,
+            torch.inference_mode(),
+        ):
+            maybe_precompile_model_kernels_after_loading(model, "cuda")
+            compile_kernel.reset_mock()
+            for tokens in (1, 17, 2048, 2049, 4097, 8192):
+                residual = torch.zeros(
+                    tokens, 4, 4096, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda"
+                )
+                if tokens <= 2049:
+                    residual.normal_(std=0.1)
+                output, comb, post, fused = layer.hc_attn_pre(
+                    residual.flatten(1),
+                    layer.input_layernorm.weight,
+                    layer.input_layernorm.variance_epsilon,
+                )
+                assert fused
+                if tokens <= 2049:
+                    ref_post, ref_comb, ref_output = mhc._mhc_pre_torch(
+                        residual,
+                        layer.hc_attn_fn,
+                        layer.hc_attn_scale,
+                        layer.hc_attn_base,
+                        1e-6,
+                        1e-6,
+                        1e-6,
+                        2.0,
+                        20,
+                    )
+                    ref_output = torch.nn.functional.rms_norm(
+                        ref_output,
+                        (4096,),
+                        layer.input_layernorm.weight,
+                        eps=1e-6,
+                    )
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(
+                        output, ref_output, atol=0.025, rtol=0.025
+                    )
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(
+                        comb, ref_comb.flatten(1), atol=0.001, rtol=0.001
+                    )
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(
+                        post, ref_post.flatten(1), atol=0.001, rtol=0.001
+                    )
+                    del ref_output, ref_comb, ref_post
+                else:
+                    assert not output.count_nonzero().item()
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(comb, torch.full_like(comb, 0.25))
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(post, torch.ones_like(post))
+                del residual, output, comb, post
+            assert compile_kernel.call_count == 0, "A warmed prefill compiled a kernel"
+    finally:
+        reset_context()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("offload_all", [True, False])
+def test_glm_mhc_prewarm_preserves_offloaded_weights(monkeypatch, offload_all):
+    """The load hook bypasses OffloaderV1's forward-time onload wrapper."""
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA is required for mHC prewarm")
+
+    publish(
+        ServerArgs(model_path="dummy", device="cuda", chunked_prefill_size=256),
+        role="test",
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mhc, "use_symmetric_memory", lambda *a, **kw: nullcontext())
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mhc, "is_allocation_symmetric", lambda: False)
+    model, layer = _make_mhc_model(sinkhorn_iters=8 if offload_all else 9)
+    layer.forward = lambda x: layer.hc_attn_pre(
+        x, layer.input_layernorm.weight, layer.input_layernorm.variance_epsilon
+    )
+    budget = 1 << 24 if offload_all else layer.hc_attn_fn.numel() * 4
+    OffloaderV1(budget).maybe_offload_to_cpu(layer)
+    assert layer.hc_attn_fn.device.type == "cpu"
+    assert layer.input_layernorm.weight.is_cuda != offload_all
+    original = [
+        (p, p.device, p.data_ptr(), p.detach().clone()) for p in layer.parameters()
+    ]
+    copies = []
+    tensor_to = torch.Tensor.to
+
+    def track_staging(tensor, *args, **kwargs):
+        result = tensor_to(tensor, *args, **kwargs)
+        if tensor.device.type == "cpu" and result.is_cuda:
+            assert result.device.index == torch.cuda.current_device()
+            copies.append(weakref.ref(result))
+        return result
+
+    jit = importlib.import_module("tilelang.jit")
+    try:
+        with (
+            get_parallel().override(tp_group=None),
+            envs.SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE.override(True),
+            patch.object(jit, "compile", wraps=jit.compile) as compile_kernel,
+            torch.inference_mode(),
+        ):
+            with patch.object(torch.Tensor, "to", track_staging):
+                maybe_precompile_model_kernels_after_loading(model, "cuda")
+            assert copies and all(ref() is None for ref in copies)
+            compile_kernel.reset_mock()
+            residual = (
+                torch.randn(17, 4, 4096, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") * 0.1
+            )
+            output, comb, post, fused = layer(residual.flatten(1))
+            assert fused and output.is_cuda
+            ref_post, ref_comb, ref_output = mhc._mhc_pre_torch(
+                residual.cpu(),
+                layer.hc_attn_fn.cpu(),
+                layer.hc_attn_scale.cpu(),
+                layer.hc_attn_base.cpu(),
+                1e-6,
+                1e-6,
+                1e-6,
+                2.0,
+                model.config.hc_sinkhorn_iters,
+            )
+            ref_output = torch.nn.functional.rms_norm(
+                ref_output, (4096,), layer.input_layernorm.weight.cpu(), eps=1e-6
+            )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(output.cpu(), ref_output, atol=0.025, rtol=0.025)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                comb.cpu(), ref_comb.flatten(1), atol=0.001, rtol=0.001
+            )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                post.cpu(), ref_post.flatten(1), atol=0.001, rtol=0.001
+            )
+            assert compile_kernel.call_count == 0, (
+                "An offloaded prefill compiled a kernel"
+            )
+            for parameter, device, pointer, value in original:
+                assert parameter.device == device and parameter.data_ptr() == pointer
+                torch.testing.assert_close(parameter, value)
+    finally:
+        reset_context()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    import sys
+
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stage CPU-offloaded mHC weights before prewarming**

When `--cpu-offload-gb` is set, `OffloaderV1` moves the decoder layer's direct mHC parameters to CPU during `make_layers`; deriving the residual device here and passing those parameters directly bypasses the layer's functional-call onload wrapper. The load hook therefore invokes the CUDA TileLang/DeepGEMM path with CPU tensors and aborts GLM startup, so prewarming must stage device copies (or skip this path) for offloaded layers.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

+    def precompile_kernels_after_loading(self) -> None:
+        """Compile the mhc_pre kernels for all split counts before serving.
+
+        mhc_pre gets its prenorm GEMM split count from the number of tokens
+        and compiles one kernel for each split count on first use. Without
+        this, eager prefills compile while the server serves. The checks
+        below give the same result on all ranks.
+        """
+        if (
+            not _is_cuda
+            or self.model is None
+            or not self.config.mhc
+            or not envs.SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE.get()
+        ):
+            return
+        # prewarm_mhc_pre gets its token counts from chunked_prefill_size.
+        chunked_prefill_size = get_schedule().chunked_prefill_size
+        if chunked_prefill_size is None or chunked_prefill_size <= 0:
+            return
+        layer = next(
+            (m for m in self.model.layers if isinstance(m, Glm5NextDecoderLayer)),
+            None,
+        )
+        if layer is None:
+            return
+        prewarm_mhc_pre(
+            # Gives dtype and device; each bucket allocates its own tokens.
+            residual=torch.zeros(
+                (1, self.config.hc_mult, self.config.hidden_size),
+                dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+                device=layer.hc_attn_fn.device,
+            ),
+            fn=layer.hc_attn_fn,

Fixed in d08f963f6. The load hook now stages only the small mHC and input-norm tensors on the rank's CUDA device, then releases them. Original parameters keep their devices and storage.

The GPU regression uses the real CPU offloader for full and partial offload. It reproduces the startup failure before the fix, then checks forward outputs and warmed kernel reuse after it. This passes locally on SM120; B200/DeepGEMM validation remains for target CI.
